webhook.event.aiSuggestionCreated: An AI suggestion was proposed (ids and the task only; nothing is applied)
webhook.event.alertRaised: An alert was raised (its type, severity, title and ids; see docs/alerts.md)
webhook.event.analyticsSynced: Analytics data was synced for an app (ids and counts only)
webhook.event.appReleaseStatusChanged: A release changed status in the store
webhook.event.appSynced: An app was synced with its store
webhook.event.asoCompetitorChanged: A followed competitor changed its listing, price or rating (ids and field names only)
webhook.event.asoCompetitorListingChange: A followed App Store competitor changed its screenshots, icon, name, description or release notes (ids and the kinds of change only)
webhook.event.asoRankChanged: A tracked keyword moved a lot in the store search results (ids and places only, never the term)
webhook.event.assetsPulled: Store images were pulled into a change set for the repository (ids and counts only)
webhook.event.authSecondFactorFailed: A second factor failed at sign-in (a wrong code after a right password; ids and a fixed reason only)
webhook.event.changesetApplied: A change set was applied (pull request opened)
webhook.event.changesetFailed: A change set could not be applied
webhook.event.ciRunFinished: A GitHub Actions workflow run finished (ids and the conclusion only)
webhook.event.ciRunStarted: A GitHub Actions workflow run started (ids only)
webhook.event.easBuildFailed: An EAS build was stored as failed (ids, platform, version and a short code only; never Expo’s message)
webhook.event.easSubmissionFailed: An EAS store submission was stored as failed (ids, platform, version and a short code only; never Expo’s message)
webhook.event.healthCrashRegression: A version crashes clearly more than the one before it (ids, version names and two rates only)
webhook.event.listingDraftPushed: Staged listing changes were written to the store as a draft (ids and counts only; never submitted)
webhook.event.listingSubmitted: A listing version was submitted for review in the store (ids only; never released)
webhook.event.memberAdded: Someone joined the workspace by accepting an invitation (ids and role)
webhook.event.pendingPublished: Pending changes were published in one go (ids, counts and the outcome of each step only)
webhook.event.planDeadlineDueSoon: A release plan’s deadline is close
webhook.event.planDeadlineOverdue: A release plan’s deadline has passed
webhook.event.planRolloutStepDone: A rollout step of a release plan was marked done
webhook.event.planRolloutStepDue: A planned rollout step’s time has passed
webhook.event.planRolloutStepReopened: A rollout step of a release plan was reopened
webhook.event.planRolloutStepSkipped: A rollout step of a release plan was skipped
webhook.event.releaseRolloutChanged: A staged rollout or phased release was changed in the store (ids and values only)
webhook.event.releaseStalled: A release looks unfinished: a build landed and the next step did not happen (ids and hours only)
webhook.event.releaseStarted: A release was started in the store: an approved version released or a Play draft rolled out (ids and values only)
webhook.event.reviewNew: A new customer review was stored, or a batch of them (ids, store and rating only; never the text)
webhook.event.reviewNewLowRating: A low-rated customer review arrived (ids and rating only)
webhook.event.reviewReplySent: A reply to a customer review was published in the store (ids only)
webhook.event.reviewUnanswered: Reviews are waiting for an answer (counts and the oldest age only)
webhook.event.stepupFailed: A confirmation of a hard action failed (wrong password or passkey)
webhook.event.stepupRecoveryUsed: A step-up recovery code was used (ids and how many are left only; never the code)
webhook.event.stepupVerified: Someone confirmed a hard action with a passkey or password
webhook.event.testflightCrash: A tester sent a TestFlight crash that was stored (ids, build and platform only; never the log)
webhook.event.testflightFeedback: A tester sent TestFlight feedback that was stored (ids, build and platform only; never the comment)
webhook.event.tokenCreated: An API token was created (its id, name and role; never the token)

webhooks.secret.verifyText: Each request has X-Kiln-Timestamp and X-Kiln-Signature headers. The signature is v1= and the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the timestamp, a dot and the raw body, keyed with the secret.
webhooks.secret.warning: Your receiver uses this secret to check that a message really came from this server. Store it in your secret manager. If it leaks, make a new one.

webhooks.table.deleteBody: {{host}} stops receiving events, and its delivery log is deleted.
webhooks.table.rotateBody: The current secret of {{host}} stops working at once, so deliveries fail verification until the receiver has the new one. You see the new secret once.
